answer: A workable defense is to make every agent solve a fresh cipher challenge bound to its own public key before it can vote or claim rewards, with the cost paid in compute time rather than money. The network then spot-checks a random sample of solutions and publishes the results, so an attacker flooding the ocean of identities with fake agents must pay that cost for each one while an honest agent pays it once. Every solved challenge leaves a public echo in the ledger, so copied or reused work is spotted at once, and identities that never do verifiable work build no reputation and earn nothing.
